en: A General Outline of the Procedures for the Avatamsaka Practice Hall (Every morning at dawn, enter the altar.
After the universal dedication of all sūtras and dhāraṇīs is completed, the reciter of the primary sūtra rises and offers incense praises; the assembly stands and recites in unison).
○ Incense Praise:
As the incense in the burner is first ignited, the entire Dharma-realm is perfumed; the assemblies of the Avataṃsaka Ocean all hear it from afar, and auspicious clouds form wherever it reaches.
As our sincere devotion grows ever more earnest, the Buddhas manifest their complete bodies.
(The Master’s text, cited from the *Baoji*, says:
The wondrous body of Vairocana pervades the Dharma-realm as his form; the Adornment of the Flower Treasury is equal in measure to the great void.
This assembly is no different from that at the site of enlightenment; the ultimate interpenetration of the environment and its inhabitants is eternally fused, whether in sages or ordinary beings.

Without interval, he first attained perfect enlightenment, manifesting spiritual transformations within the Bodhimaṇḍa; he turned the Wheel of Dharma once more, vibrating his perfect voice within the Hall of Universal Radiance.
He constantly expounded throughout the seven locations and proclaimed the teaching uniformly across the nine assemblies.

Spreading the causal flowers of the ten thousand practices and adorning the resultant fruit of the One Vehicle Path, we respectfully follow the scriptural teachings to grandly open this Dharma assembly.

We look up with reverence to pray for the consolidation of the Imperial domain, the far-reaching flourishing of the Emperor’s Way, the ever-increasing radiance of the Buddha-Sun, and the constant turning of the Wheel of Dharma. May all patrons throughout the ten directions...
May the field of merit increase; may all sentient beings of the dharma realm together realize the Buddha-wisdom of all-encompassing knowledge.
(The presiding master returns to his position.
Homage to the Flower Adornment Teacher, Vairocana Buddha. (Recite three times.)
Verse for Opening the Sutra:
The unsurpassed, most profound, and subtle Dharma, Difficult to encounter even in hundreds of thousands of millions of eons—
Now that I have seen, heard, received, and upheld it, I pray that the Tathāgata’s true meaning may be revealed.
(At the conclusion of each sutra, recite the *Mantra for Filling Gaps* [Nao] and offer praises. Alternatively, after finishing the recitation of the alphabet, perform a brief dedication as follows:
May these merits be universally extended to all; May we and all sentient beings together attain the Way of the Buddha.
(All subsequent instances shall follow this pattern.)
General Verse of Dedication:
I bow my head to the true nature-ocean of Avataṃsaka, To the Honored One of Universal Radiance,
Adorned by the myriad practices of Samantabhadra, The treasury of all suchness and the dharma-realm.
Nāgārjuna personally recited it in the Dragon Palace; Śikṣānanda expounded its subtle words in Khotan.

This wondrous Dharma-gate of the Perfect and Sudden One Vehicle, This true secret scripture for seeing one’s nature and attaining Buddhahood— Held in hand, gazed upon with eyes, and recited with mind and mouth, One should know that there must have been great karmic conditions from former lives.
Having seen, heard, and rejoiced with gladness, they have resolved upon Bodhicitta; may they ultimately and perfectly realize Sarvajñā (all-knowledge).
To all Buddhas of the ten directions and three periods of time, and to all Honored Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, [I pay homage to] the Mahāprajñāpāramitā.
(Alternatively, one may prostrate to the "Chapter on Vows" or perform the ritual of worship according to the *Huayan Wenxuan Shu* [Commentary by Wenxuan], from beginning to end.
○ At Dahuangshan in Suizhou, Chan Master Sui performed the ritual of worship for the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
Homage to the Lord of Teachings, Vairocana; to the Compassionate Honored One of the Flower Treasury World. He expounded the sūtra text of the precious verses and opened the jade casket.
Jade-axle scroll. Dust-mote after dust-mote merges; world-system after world-system is perfectly interfused.

Containing ten trillion, ninety-five thousand, four hundred and eighty characters, this is the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, the Great Vaipulya Scripture of the Buddha, the Perfect Teaching of the One Vehicle. If anyone wishes to thoroughly understand all Buddhas of the three periods of time, they should contemplate the nature of the Dharma-realm:
everything is created by the mind alone. May they always vow to make offerings and always pay reverence at the seven locations.
I constantly vow to realize and enter the teachings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the nine assemblies, and to always proclaim them;

I constantly vow to make offerings without ceasing to the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra* in its five sections and four divisions; I constantly vow to awaken to and enter the assembly of Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms of ninety lands, and to always proclaim them.
In the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, I humbly pray that in every birth and in every place,
may [so-and-so] always see such a scripture with their eyes, always hear such a scripture with their ears, always recite such a scripture with their mouths,
always transcribe such a scripture with their hands, and always realize such a scripture within their minds. May it be so!
In life after life, in every place and at every moment, may I always be able to draw near to all the holy sages of the Flower Treasury (*Gandavyūha*).
May I always receive the compassionate protection and guidance of all the holy sages of the Flower Treasury. As it is said in the Sūtra, may they all bear witness to this.
May I become like the Bodhisattva Sudhana; may I become like the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī; may I become like the Bodhisattva Maitreya; may I become like...
O Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, may I be like Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva; may I be like Vairocana Buddha.

By the merit of reciting this sutra and by the merit of making these vows, I pray that all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm of the four debts of gratitude and the three realms of existence may eliminate the immeasurable defilements and stains of their sins from beginningless time throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space. May they, together with the four...

I repay the kindness of all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm and the three realms of existence. I resolve to exhaust the immeasurable karmic enmities from beginningless time throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.

I vow that, together with all sentient beings throughout the dharma-realm and the three realms of existence—the four debts of gratitude—I shall gather immeasurable merit and wisdom from beginningless time throughout the entirety of the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, so that we may travel together through the Flower Treasury Adorned Ocean and enter [the Buddha’s enlightenment] in unison.
The Great Bodhimanda of Bodhi. Homage to the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya.
(End of the general outline for beginning and concluding the Avataṃsaka Bodhimanda practice.)
